questions.prompt: What distinguishes unconditional generation from conditional generation?

options.text: Unconditional generation does not require a task-specific conditioning input such as a class label
Unconditional generation cannot involve a trained model
Conditional generation always copies an existing file
Conditional generation necessarily changes model parameters

questions.explanation: A generative process can sample without a supplied class or prompt condition; conditional generation uses such information to guide samples.

questions.prompt: An image generator receives the label bicycle before sampling a picture. What is the label’s role?

options.text: It proves the output is a real photograph
It specifies a condition on the desired generated content
It is a confidence score for a previously supplied image
It is the complete image returned without processing

questions.explanation: The category conditions image sampling; it is neither the output nor evidence of a real-world event.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?
reference.locator: Generative versus discriminative models; p(X,Y) and p(Y|X)

questions.prompt: A classifier estimates p(label | image). Which input must be available for this prediction?

options.text: The optimizer used during the last training run
The label of every future image
The image whose label is being predicted
A newly sampled output image only

questions.explanation: A conditional label predictor uses the supplied image to estimate its category.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?
reference.locator: Generative versus discriminative models; p(X,Y) and p(Y|X)

questions.prompt: A game needs fictional terrain candidates followed by rejection of layouts with disconnected paths. Which division of responsibilities fits the task?

options.text: Train on path labels, then assume every generated candidate is connected
Retrieve a seed value and treat that value as a complete terrain
Rank invalid paths without checking whether a candidate exists
Generate candidates, then validate connectivity with a separate check

questions.explanation: Producing candidates and enforcing a structural constraint are separate operations; generation alone need not satisfy connectivity.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?
reference.locator: Generative versus discriminative models; p(X,Y) and p(Y|X)

questions.prompt: A model estimates p(image, class). Which modeling capability goes beyond estimating only p(class | image)?

options.text: Representing how the image data itself occurs together with the class
Returning a class confidence number
Accepting an image as input
Making a category prediction for an existing image

questions.explanation: Joint modeling includes the data distribution rather than only a decision about its label.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?
reference.locator: Generative versus discriminative models; p(X,Y) and p(Y|X)

questions.prompt: A product generates candidate headlines but must choose one under a fixed length rule. What does the rule contribute?

options.text: A replacement for the generation task itself
A separate acceptance constraint on generated candidates
A guarantee that every headline is factually supported
An update to the generator’s training parameters

questions.explanation: A length rule can accept or reject candidates; it does not establish truth or train the generator.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?
reference.locator: Generative versus discriminative models; p(X,Y) and p(Y|X)

questions.prompt: A model returns a number for each input. Why is that observation insufficient to classify it as generative or discriminative?

options.text: Discriminative models must return images
Every numeric output is a sampled training example
The number could describe data likelihood or a label probability; its meaning matters
Generative models cannot return numbers

questions.explanation: The modeled quantity distinguishes the tasks; the return type alone does not.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?
reference.locator: Generative versus discriminative models; p(X,Y) and p(Y|X)

questions.prompt: A system combines a generative image model with a defect classifier. Which claim about the combined system is justified?

options.text: The defect classifier becomes a generator merely by being connected to one
The generator must stop sampling once a classifier is added
Every component must estimate the same probability distribution
Its components can perform different modeling tasks within one workflow

questions.explanation: A workflow may combine candidate generation and discrimination without making their objectives identical.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?
reference.locator: Generative versus discriminative models; p(X,Y) and p(Y|X)

questions.prompt: Why can repeatedly sampling a generative model help examine its behavior?

options.text: Multiple samples reveal output variation that one sample cannot show
Each sample automatically becomes a new training update
Repeated sampling proves every example is unique
Samples expose the complete training dataset directly

questions.explanation: Sampling lets evaluators inspect variation and recurring patterns, but does not itself train or prove uniqueness.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?

questions.prompt: A model represents p(X) for data X without supplied labels. What distribution is modeled?

options.text: Only optimizer settings
The distribution of the data itself
Only class labels conditioned on X
The file-download schedule

questions.explanation: Unlabeled generative modeling can represent p(X), without requiring a class-label variable.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?

questions.prompt: A gallery contains only the best ten selected outputs from thousands of generations. What can it hide?

options.text: The existence of the ten displayed files
The fact that the model can return an image
The frequency of poor outputs in the unselected sample population
Whether any attractive output was produced

questions.explanation: Selection can hide failure frequency; evaluate an appropriately sampled population rather than only curated successes.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?

questions.prompt: A GAN emits near-identical outputs for many different random inputs. Which measurement directly assesses that pattern?

options.text: The number of characters in model filenames
The average network request latency alone
The count of optimizer configuration fields
Diversity across outputs generated from varied inputs

questions.explanation: Diversity testing examines the many-to-few mapping associated with collapsed output behavior.

questions.prompt: A conditioned generator is deliberately asked for only mountain scenes. Does the absence of beaches in these outputs establish mode collapse?

options.text: No; the condition restricts the intended output population
Yes; any restricted output category establishes collapse
Yes; conditional generators must ignore the requested category
No; mode collapse is impossible in every conditioned generator

questions.explanation: Evaluate coverage against the requested conditional distribution; restriction by design differs from unintended collapse.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?

questions.prompt: A generator produces a training image exactly, and the team claims this proves generalization. What additional distinction must be investigated?

options.text: Whether a class name appears in the filename
Memorization of examples versus performance on unseen cases
Whether the original image can be opened
Whether image bytes can be saved

questions.explanation: Reproducing a seen example alone does not demonstrate generalization beyond training cases.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?

questions.prompt: Two synthetic datasets have the same separate color and shape frequencies, but only one preserves that red items tend to be round. What differs?

options.text: Whether individual color frequencies exist
Whether the records can be serialized
The dependency between color and shape despite matching individual frequencies
The total number of feature names

questions.explanation: Matching marginal frequencies can miss relationships in the joint distribution.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?

questions.prompt: A small sample contains no rare category. Which conclusion avoids overstating the evidence?

options.text: The category is mathematically impossible for the generator
Every category must occur once in any sample
Rare-category coverage has been fully verified
Absence in a small sample does not by itself prove the model assigns that category zero probability

questions.explanation: Finite samples may omit low-frequency outcomes; coverage claims require suitable sample size and evaluation.

reference.title: Google: What is a Generative Model?

questions.prompt: What does image inpainting aim to do?

options.text: Fill or replace a specified region of an image
Transcribe speech into text
Assign a class to an entire audio recording
Train a tokenizer for source code

questions.explanation: Inpainting creates content for a targeted image region, unlike text or audio analysis.

questions.prompt: A response contains both a caption and an image. How many distinct output modalities are represented?

options.text: Zero: only input information can have a modality
Two: text and image
One: the caption replaces the image modality
Three: every word is its own modality

questions.explanation: The output contains both linguistic text and visual image information.

questions.prompt: A photo of a handwritten note is converted into machine-readable words. Which capability is central?

options.text: Video interpolation between frames
Image generation without any source input
Recognition of text from visual input
Audio synthesis from words

questions.explanation: Text recognition extracts written content from the image; it does not require synthesizing a new picture.

questions.prompt: A generated video has individually plausible frames but the same object changes appearance between adjacent frames. Which property failed?

options.text: The ability to represent still images
The existence of a text prompt
The file’s ability to contain more than one frame
Temporal consistency across frames

questions.explanation: Video quality includes continuity of content over time, beyond isolated-frame quality.

questions.prompt: A generated clip contains speech whose timing does not align with the visible speaker. Which check targets the problem?

options.text: Audio-visual synchronization
Only the average brightness of frames
Only the number of words in the input prompt
Whether the output filename ends with a video extension

questions.explanation: Alignment between sound and visual events is a separate requirement from the presence of both modalities.

questions.prompt: An app asks for image output, receives a text refusal, and attempts to display the text as image bytes. Which assumption should be corrected?

options.text: A refusal necessarily means the model accepted the editing task
The client must inspect the actual response content type before rendering
Every response to an image request necessarily contains a usable image
Any text response can be decoded as a photograph

questions.explanation: Requests can return outcomes other than the desired modality; handle the actual response and refusal path.

questions.prompt: A task asks a system to distinguish two short sound clips by the sound itself, but the app sends only their identical filenames. What information is missing?

options.text: A longer filename with no audio attached
A new response font
The audio content needed for the comparison
An image generated from each filename

questions.explanation: Metadata does not substitute for the modality containing the task-relevant evidence.

questions.prompt: A model description says it can accept video. What should be verified before relying on it for detailed audio events in a clip?

options.text: Whether the video filename contains the word sound
Whether the model can output text about any topic
Whether the service has an image-generation endpoint
Whether audio within that video is actually processed by the documented input path

questions.explanation: Video input support may differ in how visual and audio information are handled; verify the relevant input contract.

questions.prompt: What is a training loss used for?

options.text: Measuring an objective that guides parameter optimization
Storing the final generated image filename
Setting the display font of model output
Proving that an output is an authentic photograph

questions.explanation: A training loss supplies an optimization objective; it is not a factual-authenticity certificate.

questions.prompt: Why keep evaluation examples separate from model-fitting examples?

options.text: To guarantee no model can ever produce a training example
To estimate performance on data not used directly to fit parameters
To ensure evaluation itself changes every parameter
To eliminate the need to define an evaluation objective

questions.explanation: Held-out evaluation supports an assessment of generalization; it does not guarantee perfect behavior.

questions.prompt: A GAN discriminator receives authentic examples and generator-produced examples during training. What distinction does it learn?

options.text: Only image filename lengths
The optimizer’s version number
Real versus generated examples
The exact future user prompt

questions.explanation: The discriminator learns the real/generated distinction that provides adversarial feedback to the generator.

questions.prompt: An image model produces two different outputs from the same prompt with fixed weights and different random inputs. Does this establish that it retrained between requests?

options.text: Yes; every changed output requires retraining
Yes; a repeated prompt can only produce one sample
No; fixed weights imply the images must be identical
No; inference randomness can change outputs without parameter updates

questions.explanation: A fixed generative model can sample differently; output variation is not evidence of parameter updates.

questions.prompt: A team repeatedly tunes a generator using the same supposedly held-out test examples. What happens to the evaluation boundary?

options.text: Those examples influence model selection and no longer provide an independent final test
They become independent merely because their filenames say test
They are automatically excluded from all future model choices
Their use guarantees better performance on unseen data

questions.explanation: Repeated development decisions based on test outcomes compromise the independence of the final evaluation.

questions.prompt: A discriminator becomes so effective that generator learning receives very weak gradients. Which GAN training issue is relevant?

options.text: A switch from image input to audio input
Vanishing gradients
Successful convergence proved by accuracy alone
A guaranteed increase in sample diversity

questions.explanation: An overly strong discriminator can provide insufficient gradient information for generator learning.

questions.prompt: A GAN discriminator has roughly 50% accuracy on a balanced real/generated evaluation. Why is this insufficient evidence that generation is excellent?

options.text: Any balanced evaluation automatically validates all generator capabilities
A discriminator at chance cannot be evaluated using real data
The discriminator could be weak; inspect samples and broader evidence rather than treating chance accuracy as proof
Chance accuracy mathematically proves the generated data distribution is exact

questions.explanation: Difficulty distinguishing samples can result from a good generator or a poor discriminator; one metric does not prove quality.

questions.prompt: A GAN’s outputs improve briefly and then deteriorate as training continues. Which interpretation fits the documented training challenge?

options.text: Every extra training step must improve output quality
A trained generator is guaranteed to remain unchanged during training
The deterioration proves the model is performing only retrieval
Adversarial optimization may be unstable rather than steadily improving

questions.explanation: GAN training can fail to converge or destabilize; additional optimization is not an unconditional quality guarantee.

questions.prompt: A generated report omits an important limitation stated in its source. Which quality issue is present?

options.text: Incomplete coverage of relevant source information
A necessary improvement because the answer is shorter
An automatic schema-validation failure in every format
Proof that the source itself was generated

questions.explanation: Reliable reporting requires important caveats as well as correct individual statements.

questions.prompt: A tool labels a generated photograph as synthetic. What does the label communicate?

options.text: That it was retrieved unchanged from a camera archive
Its generated origin rather than proof of a photographed event
That every depicted detail is a verified real-world fact
That it cannot contain harmful content

questions.explanation: Provenance labeling helps distinguish generated media from records of real events; it does not guarantee safety or truth.

reference.title: NIST: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
reference.locator: Appendix A.1.6: Content provenance; Provenance Data Tracking Approaches

questions.prompt: A factuality check confirms every numerical value in a generated report but ignores units. Which remaining error could still matter?

options.text: A source title appearing in plain text
The response containing punctuation
A correct number paired with the wrong unit
The report using more than one paragraph

questions.explanation: Meaning depends on units and context, not only matching numerical strings.

questions.prompt: A company sends confidential customer records to a generation service without reviewing data handling. Which review is needed?

options.text: Check only whether the generated answer has a polite tone
Assume every generation endpoint has identical privacy behavior
Increase output length to compensate for sensitive input
Check the service’s data-handling policy and minimize sensitive input appropriately

questions.explanation: Privacy depends on data handling and exposure, not the wording of the generated answer.

reference.title: NIST: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
reference.locator: Section 2: Data Privacy; GV-6.1-009 vendor assessments

questions.prompt: A generated explanation accurately describes a procedure but leaves out a required warning. Which release check addresses this?

options.text: Evaluate safety-critical omissions against the intended use
Measure only whether each sentence is grammatical
Count only the number of source links
Check only the average token length

questions.explanation: Safety evaluation includes missing safeguards and warnings, not solely incorrect statements.

questions.prompt: A model gives respectful descriptions for one group but derogatory stereotypes for another. What should the team evaluate?

options.text: Whether the model uses the same network port
Group-dependent harmful bias in generated content
Only whether the response parses as text
Only how many characters each group name has

questions.explanation: Safety testing should examine harmful or unfair behavior across relevant populations.

questions.prompt: A source passage supports a claim only for adults, but the generated answer applies it to children too. Which factuality failure occurred?

options.text: The source became irrelevant because a generated answer is shorter
The claim became universally true once restated
The answer extended a claim beyond the source’s supported scope
The answer verified broader applicability by mentioning both groups

questions.explanation: Grounding requires preserving applicability conditions, not just using similar wording to a source.

questions.prompt: After deployment, users report harmful outputs on an input pattern absent from the launch tests. What response best supports ongoing reliability?

options.text: Ignore the reports because launch testing already passed
Treat reported cases as proof that every output is harmful
Disable every evaluation metric that the new cases fail
Investigate reports, add relevant regression cases and reassess mitigations

questions.explanation: Monitoring and user feedback can expose new failure patterns; incorporating them into evaluation supports iterative mitigation.
